title: Buchsbaum-Eisenbud, one direction for the last map: the maximal minors of the last map of an exact finite free complex contain a long regular sequence
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $e\ge1$ an integer, and $0\to R^{\oplus n_e}\xrightarrow{\varphi_e}R^{\oplus n_{e-1}}\xrightarrow{\varphi_{e-1}}\cdots\xrightarrow{\varphi_1}R^{\oplus n_0}$ a complex of finite free $R$-modules ($\varphi_i\circ\varphi_{i+1}=0$) [def-weil-pbc-free-module] which is exact at $R^{\oplus n_e},R^{\oplus n_{e-1}},\dots,R^{\oplus n_1}$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] (in particular $\varphi_e$ is injective). Let $A$ be the $n_{e-1}\times n_e$ matrix [def-weil-matrix] of $\varphi_e$ and let $I\subseteq R$ be the ideal generated by the $n_e\times n_e$ minors of $A$, i.e. by the determinants [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] of the $n_e\times n_e$ submatrices [def-weil-submatrix] formed by $n_e$ of the rows of $A$ (for $n_e=0$, $I=R$, the empty minor being $1$; if $n_{e-1}<n_e$ there are no such minors and $I=0$). Then either $I=R$, or $I$ contains an $R$-regular sequence $f_1,\dots,f_e$ of length $e$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence].

source.place: Algebra, Proposition Tag 00N1 (proposition-what-exact, line 24834; Buchsbaum-Eisenbud, What makes a complex exact?, Corollary 1), implication (1) => (2) for the index i = e, where (2)(a) gives rank(phi_e) = r_e = n_e so that I(phi_e) is the ideal of n_e x n_e minors (Definition Tag 00MV, definition-rank). Tag verified in tags/tags: 00N1,algebra-proposition-what-exact; 00MV,algebra-definition-rank

proof.text: (Set-up of the induction and base change of minors.) We prove, by induction on $e\ge1$, the assertion $P(e)$: for every Noetherian local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$ and every complex $0\to R^{\oplus n_e}\xrightarrow{\varphi_e}\cdots\xrightarrow{\varphi_1}R^{\oplus n_0}$ of finite free modules exact at $R^{\oplus n_e},\dots,R^{\oplus n_1}$, the ideal $I$ of $n_e\times n_e$ minors of the matrix $A$ of $\varphi_e$ is $R$ or contains an $R$-regular sequence of length $e$. Fix such data. We use throughout: if $h:R\to R'$ is a ring map and $\varphi_e\otimes_RR':R'^{\oplus n_e}\to R'^{\oplus n_{e-1}}$ is the map with matrix $h(A)$ (entries $h(a_{jk})$), then each $n_e\times n_e$ minor of $h(A)$ is $h$ of the corresponding minor of $A$ (the determinant is a polynomial with integer coefficients in the entries, and $h$ is a ring map), so the ideal of $n_e\times n_e$ minors of $h(A)$ is the ideal $IR'$ generated by $h(I)$. (For $n_e=0$ both ideals are the unit ideal; then $I=R$ and there is nothing to prove, so assume $n_e\ge1$ when convenient.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 00N1 (proposition-what-exact, line 24834), second paragraph (lines 24867-24900), implication (1) => (2)(b) for i = e

proof.text: ($I$ avoids the associated primes.) Let $\mathfrak q$ be an associated prime of $R$, $\mathfrak q=\operatorname{Ann}_R(z)$ for some $z\in R$. The localization $R_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak qR_{\mathfrak q}$, Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], and $\mathfrak qR_{\mathfrak q}$ is an associated prime of $R_{\mathfrak q}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-associated-prime-localization-depth-zero] ($R_{\mathfrak q}$ has depth $0$). Exactness of $0\to R^{\oplus n_e}\xrightarrow{\varphi_e}R^{\oplus n_{e-1}}$ (i.e. $\varphi_e$ injective) is preserved by localization [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact]; since localization commutes with finite direct sums, $(R^{\oplus n})_{\mathfrak q}=R_{\mathfrak q}^{\oplus n}$ and the localized map $\varphi_{e,\mathfrak q}:R_{\mathfrak q}^{\oplus n_e}\to R_{\mathfrak q}^{\oplus n_{e-1}}$ is injective with matrix the image of $A$ in $R_{\mathfrak q}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-depth-zero-injective-free-map-unit-minor] (Stacks 00MY with 00MW, which the source applies to the whole localized complex; only its last map is needed here) some $n_e\times n_e$ minor of this matrix is a unit of $R_{\mathfrak q}$. By Step 1 that minor is $d/1$ for an $n_e\times n_e$ minor $d\in I$ of $A$. If $I\subseteq\mathfrak q$, then $d/1\in\mathfrak qR_{\mathfrak q}$, the maximal ideal, which contains no unit. Hence $I\not\subseteq\mathfrak q$ for every associated prime $\mathfrak q$ of $R$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 00N1 (proposition-what-exact, line 24834), second paragraph (lines 24867-24900), implication (1) => (2)(b) for i = e

proof.text: (A nonzerodivisor $x\in I\cap\mathfrak m$.) If $I=R$ we are done; assume $I\neq R$, so $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ since $R$ is local. The set $\operatorname{Ass}(R)$ of associated primes of $R$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-associated-primes-finite] ($R$ is a finite $R$-module), and nonempty: by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-zerodivisors-union-associated-primes] the zerodivisors of $R$ are $\bigcup_{\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}(R)}\mathfrak q$, and $0$ is a zerodivisor ($0\cdot1=0$, $1\neq0$ in the local ring $R$). By Step 2 and prime avoidance [lem-weil-pbc-prime-avoidance] (applied to $J=I$ and the finitely many primes of $\operatorname{Ass}(R)$) there is $x\in I$ lying in no associated prime of $R$; by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-zerodivisors-union-associated-primes] $x$ is a nonzerodivisor, and $x\in I\subseteq\mathfrak m$. (The source picks $x$ in the product $I(\varphi_e)\cdots I(\varphi_1)$ to treat all $i$ at once; for $i=e$ alone $x\in I$ suffices.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 00N1 (proposition-what-exact, line 24834), second paragraph (lines 24867-24900), implication (1) => (2)(b) for i = e

proof.text: (Base case $e=1$.) If $e=1$, the one-term sequence $x$ is an $R$-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] in $I$: $x$ is a nonzerodivisor on $R$ (Step 3) and $R/xR\neq0$ because $x\in\mathfrak m$. So $P(1)$ holds.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 00N1 (proposition-what-exact, line 24834), second paragraph (lines 24867-24900), implication (1) => (2)(b) for i = e

proof.text: (Inductive step, reduction modulo $x$.) Let $e\ge2$ and assume $P(e-1)$. Put $\bar R=R/xR$; it is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian] and, as $xR\subseteq\mathfrak m$, a nonzero local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/xR$ by [lem-weil-pbc-quotient-local-structure]. By [lem-weil-pbc-free-complex-mod-nonzerodivisor-exact] (Stacks 00MZ; $x\in\mathfrak m$ is a nonzerodivisor) the complex $0\to\bar R^{\oplus n_e}\xrightarrow{\bar\varphi_e}\cdots\xrightarrow{\bar\varphi_2}\bar R^{\oplus n_1}$, with $\bar\varphi_i$ given by the matrices reduced modulo $x$, is exact at $\bar R^{\oplus n_e},\dots,\bar R^{\oplus n_2}$; it is a complex since $\bar\varphi_i\circ\bar\varphi_{i+1}$ has the reduced matrix of $\varphi_i\circ\varphi_{i+1}=0$. Renumbered as $\psi_j=\bar\varphi_{j+1}$ with terms $\bar R^{\oplus n_{j+1}}$ ($0\le j\le e-1$), it is a complex of length $e-1\ge1$ exact at all terms except the last, as $P(e-1)$ requires, and its last map $\psi_{e-1}=\bar\varphi_e$ has matrix $\bar A$. By Step 1 the ideal of $n_e\times n_e$ minors of $\bar A$ is $\bar I=I\bar R=(I+xR)/xR=I/xR$ (as $x\in I$). By $P(e-1)$, $\bar I=\bar R$ or $\bar I$ contains an $\bar R$-regular sequence $\bar y_1,\dots,\bar y_{e-1}$. The first case is impossible: $\bar I=\bar R$ would give $I+xR=R$, but $I+xR=I\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Choose $y_1,\dots,y_{e-1}\in I$ mapping to $\bar y_1,\dots,\bar y_{e-1}$ (possible since $\bar I$ is the image of $I$).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Proposition Tag 00N1 (proposition-what-exact, line 24834), second paragraph (lines 24867-24900), implication (1) => (2)(b) for i = e

proof.text: (Conclusion.) The sequence $x,y_1,\dots,y_{e-1}$ lies in $I$ and is $R$-regular [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]: $x$ is a nonzerodivisor on $R$; for $1\le j\le e-1$, $R/(x,y_1,\dots,y_{j-1})\cong\bar R/(\bar y_1,\dots,\bar y_{j-1})$ as $R$-modules, with multiplication by $y_j$ corresponding to multiplication by $\bar y_j$, which is injective; and $R/(x,y_1,\dots,y_{e-1})\cong\bar R/(\bar y_1,\dots,\bar y_{e-1})\neq0$. This is a regular sequence of length $e$ in $I$, proving $P(e)$ and the lemma.

split_report.summary: Statement kept (checked against 00N1 (1) => (2)(b) for i = e and against the citer lem-weil-pbc-residue-field-pd-le-krull-dimension step 2, which uses exactly this dichotomy for the maximal minors of the last map). Proof written from the second paragraph of the proof of 00N1, restricted to i = e: induction on e (P(e) stated in step 1); I is not in any associated prime q because, after localizing at q (depth 0, 05BZ), the injective last map has a unit maximal minor (00MY + 00MW for a two-term complex, new node); prime avoidance with Ass(R) finite (00LC) and zerodivisors = union of Ass (00LD) gives a nonzerodivisor x in I inside m; 00MZ (new node) reduces the complex mod x, the induction hypothesis gives a regular sequence of length e-1 in I/xR, and lifting it after x gives length e. Since only the last map is needed and I is the ideal of maximal minors, the rank and I(phi) of Definition 00MV are not needed (the source's rank bookkeeping only serves the other indices i < e) and x is chosen in I rather than in the product of all I(phi_i). Base change of minors, the base case and the lifting of regular sequences are elementary steps. New nodes: three Mathlib leaves (00LC, 00LD, 05BZ) and two unsplit (00MY+00MW for one injective map; 00MZ, with Mathlib candidate QuotSMulTop.map_first_exact_on_four_term_exact_of_isSMulRegular_last). lean.statement: theorem exact_free_complex_last_minors_regular_sequence (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsNoetherianRing R] [IsLocalRing R] (e : ℕ) (he : 1 ≤ e) (n : ℕ → ℕ) (φ : ∀ i : ℕ, Matrix (Fin (n (i - 1))) (Fin (n i)) R) (hcomplex : ∀ i : ℕ, 1 ≤ i → i + 1 ≤ e → ∀ v : Fin (n (i + 1)) → R, (φ i).mulVec ((φ (i + 1)).mulVec v) = 0) (hexact : ∀ i : ℕ, 1 ≤ i → i + 1 ≤ e → Function.Exact (φ (i + 1)).mulVec (φ i).mulVec) (hinjective : Function.Injective (φ e).mulVec) : let I : Ideal R := Ideal.span {d : R | ∃ r : Fin (n e) → Fin (n (e - 1)), StrictMono r ∧ d = ((φ e).submatrix r id).det} I = ⊤ ∨ ∃ rs : List R, rs.length = e ∧ (∀ x ∈ rs, x ∈ I) ∧ RingTheory.Sequence.IsRegular R rs
